docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-19

This release adds question banks: the registry package manages licensed collections of questions with immutable published versions, forks with lineage, and .h5p import and export. Question metadata gains relative difficulty, skills, and standards under the renamed h5pkit extension key. The rename is breaking; see the upgrade notes. The documentation site is reorganized into guides, design, specifications, and releases.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Question bank registry. registry.Bank, BankVersion, License, and Lineage describe licensed banks whose content lives in versions. Store persists them; MemoryStore is the in-memory implementation, and registry/registrytest is the conformance suite any other store must pass. See Question Banks.
  • Versioning. The store numbers versions, a bank has one draft at a time, and Publish validates and freezes a draft, computing the union of its questions' skills and standards. A frozen version returns ErrImmutable.
  • Forks and lineage. Fork derives a bank from a published version, recording its parent and inheriting the parent's license when it has none. Descendants finds everything derived from a bank.
  • Interop. ExportQuestionSet, ExportPackage, and WritePackage turn a version into a playable H5P question set or an .h5p package; ImportPackage reads one into a draft, keeping the metadata.
  • Question metadata. The h5pkit block adds difficultyScore (relative within a bank, 0 to 1), skills, and standards, all validated by QuestionSet.Validate. See Extensions and Standards Compliance.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
1. Rename the metadata key. The block is read and written only under extensions.h5pkit. Content with an extensions.h5pGo block no longer loads its metadata; rename the key.
  2. Rename the Go type. H5PGoExtension is now Extension and NewH5PGoExtension is now NewExtension. The old names are removed.
  3. Go 1.26. The module's go directive is 1.26.
  4. Documentation links moved. The guides are under /guides/ on the site, for example /guides/getting-started/installation/. Update bookmarks to the old paths.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No Store operation archives a version yet; archived is treated as frozen when a store sets it.
  • MemoryStore keeps everything in one process. A persistent store lives in its own module and passes registrytest.RunStoreTests.
  • The new content types (true/false, blanks, single choice set, essay, drag text, drag question) and the editor's metadata fields come in the next release.

docs.title: v0.7.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-19

This release adds Likert questions. H5P has no Likert content type, so h5pkit writes a Likert item as a standard H5P.MultiChoice question that plays ungraded in any H5P player, and records how to score it in a new scoring field on the h5pkit block. It also fixes MultiChoice behaviour fields that could not be set to false. That fix changes their Go type; see the upgrade notes.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Likert questions. QuestionSetBuilder.AddLikertQuestion writes an ordered, ungraded scale: every answer marked correct, single choice, answers in order, and checking, solutions, retry, and score points turned off. See Likert questions.
  • Scoring metadata. Extension.Scoring records the likert method, the scale, and whether an item is reverse-keyed. Extension.Validate checks it.
  • Likert validation. QuestionSet.Validate rejects a Likert question that randomizes its answers, is not single choice, shows the check button, or has an answer not marked correct. These are the settings that silently change what a respondent sees or what an answer position means.
  • Scoring by skill. QuestionSet.ScoreLikert turns chosen answers into a count, a mean, and a 0-to-1 normalized score for each skill, honoring reverse keying.
  • Behaviour fields that default to true. randomAnswers: false, enableCheckButton: false, and the other fields H5P turns on by default are now written to JSON. They were dropped, so players used their defaults.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
1. Behaviour fields are pointers. In schemas.Behaviour, EnableRetry, EnableSolutionsButton, EnableCheckButton, RandomAnswers, and ShowScorePoints are *bool. Replace RandomAnswers: true with RandomAnswers: schemas.Bool(true), and leave a field nil to use the player's default. Code that set one of these to false gets the value it asked for for the first time; check that content which relied on the old behaviour still plays as intended.
  2. Ignore H5P's score for Likert questions. Every answer is marked correct so that H5P.MultiChoice accepts the question, so the score a player or LMS reports for it is meaningless. Score with QuestionSet.ScoreLikert.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• likert is the only scoring method.
  • The TypeScript editor does not show or edit scoring yet.
  • Likert questions have not been checked inside H5P's Question Set player with the check button turned off.
  • The new content types (true/false, blanks, single choice set, essay, drag text, drag question) and the editor's metadata fields come in a later release.

docs.title: PRD — h5pkit Question Bank Registry and Documented Extensions
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-H5PKIT-001 Status: Draft Home repo: github.com/grokify/h5pkit

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
h5pkit can build, validate, serialize, and package H5P question content, and it already carries a small metadata extension (h5pGo) for section, topic, tags, difficulty, and learning objective. Two things are missing for anyone who wants to manage questions rather than only author them:

  1. There is no concept of a question bank. A QuestionSet is a playable H5P activity, not a curated, versioned, reusable collection with a license and provenance. Consumers that need banks (a learning game, a course platform, an assessment tool) each have to invent their own wrapper, and those wrappers do not interoperate.
  2. The extension is informal. Its namespace reflects a former project name, difficulty is a free string, there is no place for skill or standards alignment, and nothing documents the block as something other tools may read or write. Because H5P players ignore unknown data, the block is safe to carry, but it is only useful across tools if its shape is stable and documented.

The preference is to stay inside H5P's own approach wherever H5P has one, and to extend only where it does not, documenting each extension so that other projects can use it independently of any one consumer.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. A storage-agnostic question bank registry in h5pkit: banks, immutable published versions, licenses, fork and remix lineage, and skill and standards tags, with a Store interface and an in-memory implementation. No database dependency in h5pkit.
  2. Documented, namespaced extensions for the metadata H5P does not model: relative difficulty, skills, and standards alignment, written so a standard H5P player still imports the content unchanged.
  3. More native question types in the Go SDK: true/false, fill in the blanks, single choice set, essay, and the drag-based types that cover matching and ordering, so consumers do not invent non-H5P question formats.
  4. Round-trip interoperability: a bank version exports to a standard .h5p question set, and an imported .h5p becomes a bank version.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• A persistent (SQL or Ent) store. That belongs to the consuming application or a separate module, implementing the registry's Store interface.
  • Mastery, scoring policy, rewards, certificates, or any learner state. The registry describes content, not people.
  • A hosted registry service or marketplace. This initiative delivers the library; services are built on it.
  • Replacing H5P's per-answer feedback with a custom explanation field. H5P already models feedback natively.

docs.title: Users and Stakeholders
docs.text: Who Needs Application developers building on h5pkit Bank, version, license, and lineage types they can persist and expose without redesigning them Content authors and educators (through those applications) Difficulty, skill, and standards metadata that survives export and import Other H5P tooling A documented extension block they can read or ignore safely h5pkit maintainers Content types that follow the existing typed-params pattern and the roadmap already published

docs.title: Functional
docs.text:
• F1. A registry package defines Bank, BankVersion, License, Lineage (parent bank and version for forks and remixes), and tag types for skills and standards. Versions hold h5p.Question values.
  • F2. A published BankVersion is immutable; changing content creates a new version. Draft versions may be edited until published.
  • F3. A Store interface covers create, get, list (with filters by tag, skill, standard, license), new version, publish, and lineage lookup; an in-memory implementation and a reusable conformance test suite ship with it so other stores can prove compatibility.
  • F4. The metadata extension is renamed to the h5pkit namespace. The former h5pGo key is no longer read or written; no stored content depends on it.
  • F5. The extension gains difficultyScore (a relative score within the bank, 0 to 1), skills (identifiers in a named taxonomy), and standards (framework plus code, for example a Common Core or NGSS reference). The existing free-string difficulty label remains for display.
  • F6. Extension content is validated: score range, non-empty skill identifiers, standards with both framework and code.
  • F7. Typed parameters and builder methods for H5P.TrueFalse, H5P.Blanks, H5P.SingleChoiceSet, H5P.Essay, H5P.DragText, and H5P.DragQuestion, each validated against its semantics.
  • F8. A BankVersion exports to a QuestionSet and to a .h5p package; a .h5p question set imports to a draft BankVersion, with extension metadata preserved both ways.
  • F9. The TypeScript editor exposes the extension fields (difficulty score, skills, standards) for the types it already edits.

docs.title: Non-Functional
docs.text:
• N1. Content with the extension block loads in a standard H5P player unchanged; the extension lives beside, not inside, library parameters.
  • N2. Every extension field is documented in a guide that stands on its own, without reference to any particular consumer.
  • N3. Existing public API is preserved except for the namespace rename in F4, which is called out in release notes.
  • N4. golangci-lint passes; unit tests cover the registry, the extension validation, each new content type, and round-trip export and import.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• A consumer can create a bank, add questions with difficulty, skill, and standards metadata, publish a version, fork it into a new bank with lineage recorded, and export the version as a .h5p that a standard H5P player opens.
  • A second Store implementation (in a consumer) passes the conformance suite without changes to h5pkit.
  • The six content types in F7 round-trip through JSON and .h5p with validation.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Namespace rename breaks stored content No content depends on the old key; the release notes name the rename Extension drifts into consumer-specific fields Keep the block to content metadata; anything about learners or rewards is refused in review Content-type semantics versions move upstream Pin the library version string per type, as H5P.MultiChoice 1.16 is pinned today, and document the policy Registry grows into a service Non-goal stated; the Store interface is the boundary

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Difficulty is relative within a bank, not absolute. A score of 0.8 in an arithmetic bank is not comparable to 0.8 in a calculus bank; the documentation says so, and no cross-bank scale is implied.
  • Standards are references, not a taxonomy. h5pkit records {framework, code} pairs; it does not ship or validate the frameworks themselves.
  • Skills use caller-supplied taxonomy identifiers. h5pkit records {taxonomy, id}; the taxonomy is the consumer's.

docs.title: TRD — h5pkit Question Bank Registry and Documented Extensions
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-H5PKIT-001

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
• Package h5p (module root): QuestionSet, Question{Library, Params, Extensions}, MultiChoiceQuestion with typed schemas.MultiChoiceParams, a QuestionSetBuilder whose only question method is AddMultipleChoiceQuestion, JSON round-trip, Validate, and .h5p package create and load.
  • Extensions{H5PGo *H5PGoExtension} serialized under the JSON key h5pGo, with Section, Topic, Tags, Difficulty string, QuestionNumber, LearningObjective, Source, and Custom map[string]any.
  • schemas/: typed params and semantics for multiple choice; semantics JSON only for true/false and essay.
  • semantics/: generic semantics field model.
  • ts/packages/editor: React editor for multiple choice, true/false, and fill in the blanks.
  • Published roadmap lists essay, true/false, and single choice set as short-term content types and a content marketplace as long-term.

docs.title: 1. Extension namespace and fields
docs.text:
Rename the block to the h5pkit key and give it a documented shape:

type Extensions struct {
    H5PKit *Extension `json:"h5pkit,omitempty"`
}

type Extension struct {
    Section           string         `json:"section,omitempty"`
    Topic             string         `json:"topic,omitempty"`
    Tags              []string       `json:"tags,omitempty"`
    Difficulty        string         `json:"difficulty,omitempty"`        // display label
    DifficultyScore   *float64       `json:"difficultyScore,omitempty"`   // 0..1, relative within a bank
    Skills            []SkillRef     `json:"skills,omitempty"`
    Standards         []StandardRef  `json:"standards,omitempty"`
    QuestionNumber    int            `json:"questionNumber,omitempty"`
    LearningObjective string         `json:"learningObjective,omitempty"`
    Source            string         `json:"source,omitempty"`
    Custom            map[string]any `json:"custom,omitempty"`
}

type SkillRef    struct { Taxonomy, ID string }
type StandardRef struct { Framework, Code string }
  • The h5pGo key is neither read nor written, and Extensions uses the default JSON encoding.
  • Validation: DifficultyScore in [0,1]; each SkillRef has non-empty Taxonomy and ID; each StandardRef has non-empty Framework and Code. Validate on QuestionSet calls it.
  • The block stays a sibling of library and params on the question (as today), so H5P players never see it inside library parameters.

docs.title: 2. registry package
docs.text:
github.com/grokify/h5pkit/registry, no dependency beyond the root package and the standard library.

type Bank struct {
    ID          string
    Slug        string
    Title       string
    Description string
    Subject     string
    Language    string          // BCP 47
    License     License
    Tags        []string
    Lineage     *Lineage        // nil for an original bank
    CreatedAt, UpdatedAt time.Time
}

type BankVersion struct {
    BankID      string
    Version     string          // semantic version
    Status      Status          // draft | published | archived
    Questions   []h5p.Question
    Skills      []h5p.SkillRef     // union of question skills, computed on publish
    Standards   []h5p.StandardRef  // union, computed on publish
    Notes       string
    PublishedAt *time.Time
}

type License struct {
    SPDX        string          // e.g. CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, proprietary
    Attribution string
    URL         string
}

type Lineage struct {
    ParentBankID  string
    ParentVersion string
    Relation      Relation      // fork | remix | translation
}

Immutability. Publish sets Status = published, computes the skill and standards unions, and freezes the version; any mutation on a published version returns ErrImmutable. New content means NewVersion(bankID, from version) which copies questions into a draft.

Store.

type Store interface {
    CreateBank(ctx, Bank) (Bank, error)
    GetBank(ctx, id) (Bank, error)
    ListBanks(ctx, ListFilter) ([]Bank, error)        // tag, skill, standard, license, subject, language, lineage
    NewVersion(ctx, bankID, fromVersion string) (BankVersion, error)
    SaveDraft(ctx, BankVersion) error                 // ErrImmutable if published
    Publish(ctx, bankID, version string) (BankVersion, error)
    GetVersion(ctx, bankID, version string) (BankVersion, error)
    ListVersions(ctx, bankID) ([]BankVersion, error)
    Fork(ctx, parentBankID, parentVersion string, into Bank, rel Relation) (Bank, BankVersion, error)
    Descendants(ctx, bankID) ([]Bank, error)
}

MemoryStore implements it. registry/registrytest exports RunStoreTests(t, func() Store) so any implementation (an Ent store in a consumer, for example) proves conformance.

docs.title: 3. Interop
docs.text:
• registry.ExportQuestionSet(v BankVersion, opts) (*h5p.QuestionSet, error) builds a playable set; ExportPackage wraps it in an .h5p with the required library dependencies.
  • registry.ImportPackage(path) (BankVersion, error) loads an .h5p question set into a draft version, preserving extension blocks.

docs.title: 4. Content types
docs.text:
Follow the existing pattern (schemas.MultiChoiceParams + Validate, NewMultiChoiceQuestion, builder method), one typed params struct per library, library version pinned in a constant:

Library Covers Builder method H5P.TrueFalse true/false AddTrueFalseQuestion H5P.Blanks fill in the blanks AddBlanksQuestion H5P.SingleChoiceSet rapid single-choice sets AddSingleChoiceSet H5P.Essay free text with keyword scoring AddEssayQuestion H5P.DragText ordering and word matching AddDragTextQuestion H5P.DragQuestion drag and drop, image matching AddDragQuestion

Semantics JSON for each is added to schemas/ from the upstream library at the pinned version, with a test that the typed params validate against it. Library version strings are confirmed against the upstream releases at implementation time, not assumed.

docs.title: 5. TypeScript editor
docs.text: Add an "Metadata" section to the existing editor for difficulty score, skills, and standards, reading and writing the h5pkit block. No new question types in the editor in this initiative; the Go SDK leads.

docs.title: 6. Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/guides/user-guide/extensions.md: the block, every field, the relative-difficulty rule, the h5pkit key, and how another tool should treat the block.
  • docs/guides/user-guide/question-banks.md: registry concepts, immutability, lineage, conformance suite, and interop.
  • docs/guides/reference/standards.md: replace the placeholder with how StandardRef is used and the H5P specification points h5pkit follows.
  • docs/guides/development/roadmap.md: mark the content types delivered and link the registry.

docs.title: 7. Versioning
docs.text: Release the extensions and the registry as v0.6.0, Likert scoring as v0.7.0, and the content types and the editor metadata in the next minor release after that. Likert scoring makes the MultiChoice behaviour fields that default to true *bool, which is breaking. The namespace rename and the Extension type rename are breaking changes; everything else is additive. The go directive is raised to the organization's current minimum as part of the release item, subject to CI toolchain availability.

docs.title: Sequencing Constraints
docs.text:
• §1 before §2 (the registry computes unions from SkillRef and StandardRef).
  • §2 before §3 (interop operates on BankVersion).
  • §4 is independent of §1–§3 and can run in parallel.
  • §5 depends on §1.
  • §6 and §7 last.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Upstream semantics drift. Pinning per library and testing typed params against the pinned semantics JSON catches it at upgrade time.
  • Custom as an escape hatch. Document that Custom is for consumer-private data and is never interpreted by h5pkit or the registry; resist adding typed fields for one consumer's needs.
  • Over-modeling the registry. Keep Bank to what every consumer needs; consumer-specific fields go in the consumer's persistence layer, keyed by Bank.ID.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Extension: JSON round-trip under the h5pkit key; validation table tests.
  • Registry: registrytest suite run against MemoryStore; immutability, version copy, fork lineage, filter semantics.
  • Interop: export then import yields an equal BankVersion (ignoring timestamps and status); exported .h5p passes the existing package validation.
  • Content types: params validation against pinned semantics; builder output round-trips through JSON.
  • Editor: component tests for the metadata section.
